thread:
noah: FYI we finished a small canary for the adaptive batcher + compact-kernel combo. Good wins overall :tada:

tara: Topline numbers?

noah: p50 -9%, p95 -14%, p99 -16% on mixed-generation benchmark (seq~128). Token compute cost down ~5.5% on canary slice.

ryan: Which workloads saw the most improvement?

noah: Short-turn dialogue and multi-turn assistants benefited most due to better packing. Large single-shot prompts saw minimal change.

bench-bot: Canary summary: 24h, 4% traffic, env=prod-canary. GPU utilization up 6% efficient, avg latency -8%. Report: https://redwood-internal/bench/reports/1890001111

ryan: Any correctness or stability issues?

noah: No correctness regressions. We observed jitter on a small subset of GPU nodes during heavy GC; mitigated by adjusting per-worker batch cap and a quick kernel warmup.

ops-bot: Guard set: runtime/compact_kernel/p99_delta > 12% -> auto-fallback.

tara: Rollout plan?

noah: Ramp 4%->20%->50%->100% over 72h with automated gating at each step. Adding runtime dashboard tiles: "Adaptive Batcher Efficiency" and "Compact Kernel Savings".

ryan: Can we get a one-liner for release notes?

noah: Draft: "Adaptive batching + compact kernels reduce p95 latency by ~10-15% for dialogue workloads and lower token compute by ~5% for reuse-heavy traffic."

tara: Thanks — please drop slides for all-hands.

noah: Will do.
